title: feat: project manager sets area, type and priority
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds a single brief, `operations/github/project-manager.md`: 15 focus areas, issue types and priority rules. The classifier and the team read the same file
- Every new issue and PR gets an Area and Source in the Dev project; issues also get a GitHub issue type (Bug, Feature, Question, Task) and Priority (High, Medium, Low)
- Area follows what the merged code does; where work came from (for example a quest) doesn't decide it. Promotion PRs get their Area cleared, census responses are skipped, app submissions get App catalog & showcase without an AI call
- One flow for issues and PRs; Dev fields are looked up by name. Removes classifier labels, tracking parents, the Discord user map and the paid-customer priority bump
- Adds a separate job every 30 minutes that moves recent issues from paying customers to the new Express priority, only after the classifier has set one
- Drops the `BILLING` label from the balance issue template and updates AGENTS.md and the issue-maker skill

Tested with log-only runs from this branch on 38 mixed issues and PRs (0 failures) and 300 merged PRs (88% agreement with an earlier manual sort). The Express job was dry-run locally against 212 recent issues. The org issue types and Dev field options already match.

gist.headline: A place for every issue
gist.blurb: The Dev project gets a tidier sorting system: one shared brief guides both the classifier and the humans reading its work. Even the express lane waits its turn.
gist.summary: A shared 15-area project-manager brief guides classification of new issues and PRs into Dev project Area and Source fields; issues also receive a type and priority, with a separate 30-minute job assigning Express priority to eligible issues after classification.
gist.impact: Maintainers get consistent project fields for incoming work, while eligible customer issues can move to Express priority without bypassing their initial classification.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the Dev project as a cozy garden sorting board: issue and PR cards go into clearly marked Area and Source planters, with a small Express path branching off after the main sorting station. Polli checks the cards with a clipboard while the monitor robot helps sort them; the visual is about orderly maintainer workflow, not a new user-facing feature.
